summary.description: Bing Bong protects a true friend.
rules: On the first night, Bing Bong learns one player chosen by the Storyteller: their *REAL FRIEND*.
The first time the real friend would die, Bing Bong dies instead.
From then on, the real friend can no longer change alignment, and may be protected from death at Storyteller discretion.

howToRun: On the first night, mark one player *REAL FRIEND*. Wake Bing Bong and point to that player.
When the real friend would die, keep them alive, kill Bing Bong instead, and mark the friend *SAFE?*.
From then on, prevent all alignment changes to the real friend, and any time they would die, they might not.
howToRunExamples: Choose a real friend whose survival creates an interesting relationship. Avoid selecting a player whose unavoidable early death makes Bing Bong's game purely automatic.
examples: The Demon attacks the real friend. Bing Bong dies instead and the friend remains alive and good.
The real friend is executed. Bing Bong dies, and the Storyteller keeps the friend alive. The execution still happened, and the day still ended.
After Bing Bong's sacrifice, the Mezepheles tries to turn the real friend evil. They remain their current alignment.
tipsAndTricks: Tell your real friend! You exist to die for them.
Stay hidden otherwise! You do nothing if you are killed before your friend.
Your friend will be more trustworthy after you die in their place. Don't be afraid to die to supercharge your team.
Stick with your friend! Nothing stops a Mezepheles from turning them before you die saving them.
opposingTips: The Storyteller can't kill you in place of your "friend", since you aren't actually Bing Bong. Be prepared to bluff Drunk, or claim that a Vortox is in play. Your "friend" might look suspicious if they die without you dying, but they are already dead. You are always going to look more suspicious!
If you're likely to die at night, such as being an Imp, Fang Gu, or have an allied Vigormortis, you might want to claim Bing Bong to add credibility to a teammate.

summary.description: The Secretary knows two in-play characters, but not who they are.
rules: On the first night, the Secretary learns exactly two in-play characters.
The Secretary learns characters, not players or alignments.
The two characters may be good or evil and may include characters that misregister as in play.
If fewer than two legal distinct characters can be shown, the Storyteller may show the same character only when multiple instances exist.

howToRun: During setup, mark two in-play characters *KNOW*. Prefer a pair which indicates what kind of game is to be solved.
On the first night, wake the Secretary and show both character tokens. Put the Secretary to sleep.
examples: Charlie the Secretary sees Chef and Imp. When only a single player claims Chef, they know to believe the claim.
The Secretary sees Drunk and Poisoner. They know that people with bad information or malfunctionabilities are likely to still be good.
tipsAndTricks: See what claims come out. Your information is most valuable when evil doesn't know what to double claim.
An evil character token is especially valuable. You know what kind of Minion disruption, or even characteristic Demon, is in play.
You are not the King! If you enter play mid-game, you might see the character of a dead player.
opposingTips: Back up good claims. Confirm yourself!
Back up evil bluffs. Confirm your teammates!
Claim the unknowable! Drunk or Mutant can cast doubt on everyone's information! But be prepared when time passes without any dead player claiming Mutant.

summary.description: The Quitter blindly stakes everything on one player.
rules: On the first night, the Quitter chooses a player other than themself.
If that player later dies for any reason, the Quitter permanently loses the ability to vote on nominations.
The Quitter gives up even when dead. They then may no longer use their dead vote.
The Quitter may still nominate, speak, and sincerely try.

howToRun: On the first night, wake the Quitter. They choose another player. Mark that player *ONLY HOPE*.
When the chosen player dies, mark the Quitter *RAGE QUIT!*.
From then on, do not count any vote from the Quitter. Remind them discreetly if they raise a hand.
howToRunExamples: As with the Butler or Zealot, the Quitter cannot know if they are drunk or poisoned. Voting when they cannot is considered cheating!
examples: The chosen player is killed by the Demon. The Quitter cannot vote for the rest of the game.
The Quitter dies first. They may still use their dead vote until their chosen player dies. If their chosen player dies, they cannot vote at all.
The chosen player changes character. They are still the Quitter's only hope.
tipsAndTricks: Tell your chosen player! If they die freely, you will be severely limited.
Your chosen is not necessarily your ally. In fact, the best case scenario is that you picked the Demon, and you'll be free to act all game!
You don't need to actually give up! You can still coordinate, discuss, and nominate. In the end, you might end up making the winning nomination.
opposingTips: You can claim Quitter while remaining cagey about your chosen. If you must abstain, you can explain that you have lost your only hope, and can't vote.
Be vague about you believing that killing your teammates is a bad idea. People that have heard your claim of Quitter may back off.

You don't need to be a complete method actor. If you would win, you are not a real Quitter, and can cast a decisive vote. If the game doesn't end, you could always try to claim to have been locked by a Cerenovus.
